name: Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex
description: The California station of NASA's Deep Space Network, managed by JPL, which tracks and communicates with interplanetary spacecraft. It is one of three DSN sites spaced about 120 degrees apart around the Earth.
highlights: Its 70 m antenna DSS-14, the 'Mars' dish, was upgraded from 64 m in 1988 to support Voyager and keeps contact with Voyager 1.
The original 26 m Pioneer station (DSS-11) became a National Historic Landmark in 1985.
When not tracking spacecraft its antennas also map quasars and do planetary radar.
